ROLE: Append the fixed two-byte PINGRESP packet 0xD0 0x00 to a caller-owned output buffer.

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: destination for the encoded packet bytes

FUNC.NAME: buffer_reserve
FUNC.ROLE: allocate the two packet bytes in one step

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_reserve
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when cap >= len + 2; -1 on overflow or allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no transfer; the buffer keeps or grows its storage
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means no byte was written and the contents are unchanged, so the caller returns -2

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_append
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int buffer_append(struct byte_buf *buf, const void *src, size_t len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when the bytes were appended; -1 when nothing was appended
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no transfer; the two bytes are copied
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: cannot fail after the reserve covered both bytes; a -1 is propagated as -2

LOGIC.INPUT: out: caller-owned output buffer that receives exactly two bytes (a PINGREQ was validated by the caller).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out is NULL return -1 (nothing written). 2) If buffer_reserve(out, 2) != 0 return -2 (allocation failure; contents unchanged). 3) byte0 = (WIRE_PACKET_PINGRESP << 4) | 0x00 = 0xD0; byte1 = 0x00 (Remaining Length 0); buffer_append(out, &byte0, 1); buffer_append(out, &byte1, 1). Both appends are guaranteed to succeed after the reserve; if one returns -1, return -2 and let the caller discard the buffer. 4) Return 0. The response is appended to the queue, so business traffic queued earlier or later is unaffected and keeps its order (scope R09: the connection continues after a PINGRESP).
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when exactly 0xD0 0x00 was appended and out->len grew by 2; -1 for a NULL out with nothing written; -2 when the buffer could not be grown.
INVARIANTS_USED: PINGRESP has type 13, reserved flags 0 and Remaining Length 0 (MQTT-3.13.1-1)
the response is queued, not sent inline, so a slow socket never blocks the event loop
a queue append preserves the relative order of queued packets
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: out is NULL or a valid byte_buf owned by the caller.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: on success the last two bytes of out are 0xD0 0x00; on failure no complete packet is appended.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe; the caller owns out exclusively.

WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: 0xD0: type 13 in the high nibble, reserved flag bits 0 in the low nibble.
0x00: PINGRESP has no variable header and no payload, so the packet is exactly two bytes.

EXPECT.note: the queued CONNACK is preserved and the PINGRESP follows it

calls: byte_buf out; buffer_init(&out); force buffer_reserve to fail
